problem_severity_frequency.rationale: The new buying surface is real and dated, but merchant-side pain, urgency and frequency are not evidenced; the sourced material shows supply-side platform action, not buyer pain.

buyer_budget_clarity.rationale: Buyer identified (off-platform merchants/agencies) but no evidence they hold or would allocate a budget for agent-readiness; platforms give it away.

evidence_strength.rationale: Primary platform/payment-provider sources establish the change and the bundled competitive response, but no demand-side evidence.

distribution.rationale: Only plausible agency/marketplace routes; no non-paid route to early buyers evidenced (capped at 2 for plausible-only distribution).

differentiation.rationale: Readiness is bundled free by Shopify/Google/Stripe/OpenAI and the protocols are open; direct incumbent overlap.

validation_speed_cost.rationale: A price/integration test would be cheap, though the hard-filter fail makes a test unjustified.

feasibility.rationale: Integration work is well documented and technically straightforward for a commerce engineer.

economics.rationale: Modelled only and untested (capped at 2); competing with a free bundled offer erodes pricing power.

founder_fit.rationale: Inferred fit for a commerce-integration engineer with agency relationships; no owner-specific evidence.

risk.rationale: Platform dependence and protocol churn are the main risks; no acute legal/privacy risk identified.

economic_buyer.note: A buyer segment is identifiable but budget allocation for this job is not evidenced.
economic_buyer.resolve_via: Test whether off-platform merchants or their agencies will pay for agent-readiness.

painful_frequent_or_budgeted.note: Potential lost sales are plausible but no buyer-side pain or budget evidence.
painful_frequent_or_budgeted.resolve_via: Interview off-platform merchants about AI-channel sales and current spend.

non_paid_distribution.note: Agency referrals and marketplace listings are plausible, not evidenced.
non_paid_distribution.resolve_via: Test one non-paid channel (e.g. agency partnership) for reachable buyers.

defensible_wedge.note: Platforms and payment networks bundle agent-readiness free (Shopify/Google UCP, OpenAI/Stripe ACP, PayPal, WooCommerce), the protocols are open-sourced, and the function is a feature of commerce platforms.

no_network_effects_needed.note: Value may not require density, but merchant-side adoption dynamics were not tested.
no_network_effects_needed.resolve_via: Assess whether value holds for a single merchant without platform-wide adoption.

plausible_margins.note: No cost or price evidence gathered.
plausible_margins.resolve_via: Model integration and support cost against a tested price.

acceptable_risk.note: Platform/protocol dependence is the main risk; not assessed in depth.
acceptable_risk.resolve_via: Review platform terms and protocol governance before any build.

cheap_disconfirming_test.note: A cheap test is conceivable but was not specified because the wedge already fails.

not_all_optimistic.note: Any viable path would require many favourable assumptions at once against subsidised incumbents.
